name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with congenital heart disease
aliases: Congenital heart disease-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ESC/ERS Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension

criteria.description: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) ≥ 25 mmHg at rest measured by right heart catheterization
Confirmed diagnosis of congenital heart disease with systemic-to-pulmonary shunt or repaired defect with residual pulmonary hypertension
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension such as left heart disease or lung disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Hemodynamic confirmation of pulmonary arterial hypertension by right heart catheterization in the presence of congenital heart disease and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, imaging, and hemodynamic data.

pathognomonic.notes: Progressive shortness of breath on exertion
Transient loss of consciousness related to decreased cardiac output
Central or peripheral bluish discoloration due to hypoxemia

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

common.notes: Swelling of lower limbs due to right heart failure
Non-specific chest pain related to right ventricular strain

occasional.notes: Coughing up blood due to pulmonary vascular rupture
Enlarged liver secondary to right heart failure
Redness of palms due to vascular changes

rare.notes: Enlargement of distal phalanges due to chronic hypoxia

rare.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression
rare.notes: Voice changes caused by enlarged pulmonary arteries
searchTerms: voice changes due to nerve pressure

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP indicating right ventricular strain
Mild polycythemia due to chronic hypoxia
imaging: Echocardiography showing right ventricular hypertrophy and elevated pulmonary artery pressures
Chest X-ray demonstrating enlarged pulmonary arteries and right heart enlargement
Cardiac MRI for detailed assessment of right ventricular function
Right heart catheterization confirming elevated pulmonary arterial pressures and vascular resistance
genetic: Mutations in BMPR2 gene may be present in some cases of PAH
Other genetic variants associated with pulmonary arterial hypertension
other: Electrocardiogram showing right axis deviation and right ventricular hypertrophy
6-minute walk test demonstrating reduced exercise capacity

redFlags: Signs of right heart failure such as severe peripheral edema and ascites
Hemoptysis indicating possible pulmonary artery rupture
references: Galiè N, Humbert M, Vachiery JL, et al. 2015 ESC/ERS Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Heart J. 2016 Jan 1;37(1):67-119.
Simonneau G, Montani D, Celermajer DS, et al. Haemodynamic definitions and updated clinical classification of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Respir J. 2019 Jan 24;53(1):1801913.
Orphanet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with congenital heart disease. ORPHA:275803.
